sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Chad
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 7 September 2026; reports crop conditions through mid-August 2026 and outcomes for the 2025 cereal season.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS combines cereal-balance, price, Cadre Harmonisé and satellite crop-monitoring information.
sources.limitations: This dated brief is a snapshot; its 2026 seasonal outlook is not a verified final harvest result.

sources.title: When the Waters Rise: How the City of N’Djamena, Chad, Prepared for Floods and Averted Disaster
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank results brief on the N’Djamena Urban Resilience Project's 2024 flood-preparedness activities and reported results, published 26 May 2026.
sources.methodology: World Bank results brief describes PILIER activities and reported 2024 results.
sources.limitations: Project results are self-reported; the page provides no counterfactual or independent evaluation of flood losses avoided.

sources.title: Chad Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF report published 9 February 2026, covering 1 January to 31 December 2025 and summarizing humanitarian needs and response.
sources.limitations: Some OCHA data are relayed; flood data lack household detail.

sources.title: Chad Situation Report #1 – July 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: UNFPA report on the July 2024 humanitarian situation, published August 2024.
sources.methodology: UNFPA operational situation report summarizing reported flood impacts, displacement and service delivery.
sources.limitations: The brief gives no named flood-affected provinces or detailed breakdown of affected women and girls.

claims.locator: Section ‘Uncertain production prospects for 2026 cereal crops’, paragraphs on rainy-season onset and vegetation conditions.
claims.paraphrase: FAO’s 7 September 2026 brief reports that erratic rains and dry spells left poor satellite vegetation conditions by mid-August in Logone Occidental, Logone Oriental, Mandoul, Moyen-Chari, Lac, Batha, Wadi Fira and Ouaddaï.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: This is a dated crop-condition snapshot, not a final yield or household-loss estimate.

claims.locator: Section ‘Cereal output in 2025 estimated at above-average level’.
claims.paraphrase: FAO estimated 2025 cereal output at 3 million tonnes, 10% above its five-year average, but reported lower output in parts of the Sudanian zone and localized shortfalls where civil insecurity disrupted farming in Lac and southern areas.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: The national estimate masks local variation; FAO gives no province-level loss amounts.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO says civil insecurity disrupted farming in Lac and southern areas and caused localized production shortfalls; it does not estimate an interaction with rainfall.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section ‘Cereal output in 2025 estimated at above-average level’, final sentence.

claims.locator: ‘Development Challenge’ section, paragraph on N’Djamena’s flood risk.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank says N’Djamena, at the Chari–Logone confluence, faces high flood risk from intense rains, rapid urban growth, clogged drains and limited emergency capacity; risk heightened after the 2022 floods and ahead of the 2024 rainy season.
claims.limitations: The page describes citywide risk drivers but does not estimate exposure or impacts by neighborhood.

claims.locator: ‘Results Highlights’ and ‘World Bank Group Approach’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank reports that 2024 PILIER works cleared and repaired 350 km of N’Djamena drains, deployed 12 pumps, trained about 30 technicians, and provided neighborhood maps and pre-positioned supplies benefiting 9,858 households; the city remained largely unharmed during high river levels.
claims.limitations: These are World Bank-reported outputs and results; the page provides no counterfactual estimate of losses prevented.

claims.locator: ‘Situation Overview and Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph beginning ‘Chad continued to rank’.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports 2025 floods killed people and displaced residents in Mandoul, Moyen-Chari, Salamat and Wadi Fira; the season was milder than 2022 and 2024.
institutions: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
claims.limitations: No province-level losses or household estimates are given.

claims.locator: ‘Situation Overview and Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph beginning ‘In 2025, OCHA recorded’.
claims.paraphrase: Citing OCHA, UNICEF says access restrictions prevented assessment or aid during displacement events in Logone Occidental, Ouaddaï and Mayo Kebbi Ouest; armed groups remained active on Lake Chad islands.
institutions: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
claims.limitations: OCHA attribution; events are not linked to flooding.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Access restrictions prevented aid and assessment during major displacement.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: ‘Situation Overview and Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph beginning ‘In 2025, OCHA recorded’.

claims.locator: ‘Situation Overview and Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph on 2025 flooding and preparedness.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports that the Humanitarian Country Team supported a national contingency plan and stocks after 2025 floods.

claims.locator: Opening situation summary, paragraph beginning ‘At the end of July 2024’.
claims.paraphrase: UNFPA reports torrential July 2024 rains flooded western and southern Chad, affecting over 6,300 people and displacing some; it says displacement would impede women’s and girls’ service access and increase protection risks amid broader insecurity and intercommunal tensions.
claims.limitations: The brief gives no named provinces or detailed affected-population breakdown; its security context is not attributed to flooding.

access_audit.locator: Full GIEWS brief, especially the 2026 crop-prospects section and 2025 output section; reference date 7 September 2026.
access_audit.notes: The whole accessible page was read. Seasonal statements are tied to the brief's reference date and not treated as verified final 2026 harvest results.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.locator: Full World Bank results brief, especially ‘Results Highlights’, ‘Development Challenge’ and ‘World Bank Group Approach’.
access_audit.notes: The public results page was read in full; outcome descriptions are attributed to the World Bank and not treated as an independent impact evaluation.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank copyright; no separate open license verified.

access_audit.locator: Full 15-page report, ‘Situation Overview and Humanitarian Needs’, including the 2025 flood and access-restriction paragraphs.
access_audit.notes: The full official UNICEF PDF text was read. The access-restriction figures are attributed in the report to OCHA's January–September 2025 overview.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.locator: Full UNFPA public situation-report page, opening situation summary and response paragraph.
access_audit.notes: The page was read in full. The passage states that flooding heightened gendered service-access and protection risks; it does not attribute security instability to floods.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.notes: Direct page opening returned 403. No claims rely on search excerpts.

access_audit.locator: SPARC technical report, license statement on PDF p. 2; Dar Sila retrospective study, 21 pages.
access_audit.notes: The public report was fully inspected, but substantive findings were excluded from claims because the displayed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms prohibit derivatives; only the license/access audit is retained.

search_audit.query: Chad 2024 floods province Lac displacement food security climate vulnerability OCHA WFP UN report 2025
search_audit.outcome: Found FAO's September 2026 crop-condition update with eight named provinces, UNICEF's 2025 report on provincial floods and displacement, and a World Bank results brief on N’Djamena.

search_audit.query: Chad Lake Chad climate shocks livelihood insecurity conflict mediator explicit mechanism source report 2024 2025
search_audit.outcome: Accessible FAO and UNICEF reporting names insecurity as a driver of agricultural shortfalls or humanitarian access constraints, but does not establish that climate hazards caused violence. A 2026 Lake Chad research PDF timed out and was not used.

search_audit.query: Chad Lake Province armed conflict insecurity disrupted flood adaptation climate resilience humanitarian access report 2024 2025
search_audit.outcome: FAO says civil insecurity disrupted farming in Lac and some southern areas; UNICEF, citing OCHA, reports access restrictions preventing assistance during displacement events. Neither establishes violence blocking a named climate-adaptation project.

search_audit.query: Chad local community climate resilience flood adaptation project outcomes Lac N'Djamena Logone Chari 2024 2025 report
search_audit.outcome: Found World Bank-reported N’Djamena drainage, pumping, technician training and neighborhood preparedness results, and UNICEF's national contingency-planning and stock measures. The inspected SPARC report used CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms and its findings were not extracted.

gaps: No inspected source establishes a climate-to-violence causal pathway in Chad; co-occurrence of climate hazards, insecurity and displacement is not treated as causation.
FAO's September 2026 crop brief is a dated seasonal snapshot; its 2026 outlook was not treated as a verified final harvest result.

UNICEF's 2025 flood paragraph provides named provinces but no household-level loss estimates; its access restrictions are cited from an OCHA overview and relate to displacement events not linked to flooding.
The World Bank's N’Djamena results brief attributes preparedness outcomes to PILIER but gives no independent counterfactual estimate of losses avoided.
The March 2026 Lake Chad research PDF timed out and the IOM May 2026 DTM page returned 403; no findings from their search excerpts were used.
SPARC's Dar Sila retrospective report was read but substantive findings were excluded because its stated CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms prohibit derivatives.
